terms.meaning: A file of style rules that control how a page looks.
A named design value, such as a colour or font, shared across the site.
A rule that applies only when the screen is a certain width.
A rule that matches elements by an attribute, such as a test-id label.
A position that stays on screen while the page scrolls.
A label placed on an element so automated tests can find it.
The list showing each stage of a processing run and its status.

depends_on: Shared colour and font value files (not in the packet)
used_by: Public site and workspace page components (paths not in the packet)

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Base layout for front page and headers
sections.what: Sets the look of the public front page: the dark header with logo and links, the hero block with a large heading and photo shade, buttons, the four-column tool grid with image overlays and hover zoom, and the footer. Most colours come from shared named values rather than fixed colours.
sections.why: The top comment says the design uses dark chrome with light content, and that all colours come from shared tokens.
sections.watch_out: A missing or renamed shared colour value leaves text or backgrounds without their intended colour, with no error.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Overview, steps, workspace and pipeline styles
sections.what: Styles the overview and numbered steps, related links, industry banners and sector buttons. Then it styles the workspace page with its scope picker, selection basket and workspace header. It ends by starting the pipeline trace, a stage list whose side rail has a fixed height and scrolls.
sections.why: Likely reason: the workspace header is set to stay on screen while scrolling, and the stage list has its own scroll area.
sections.watch_out: Several workspace rules find elements by test-id labels, so renaming one of those labels silently removes its styling.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Stage tracker dots and status colours
sections.what: Styles the small circle marker, label and detail text for each step of a pipeline view. The colour of each step changes with its status, such as done, running, failed or insufficient evidence. It also styles the detail panel under the steps, including the findings list and a dark box for log output.
sections.why: Likely reason: the status colour is picked from a data-status attribute, so one set of rules covers every step.
sections.watch_out: The status names in these rules must match the names the app writes, or the colours will silently not appear.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 767px)
sections.title: Phone layout for the stage view
sections.what: On screens up to 767 pixels wide, the stage view becomes one column. The step list sits above the detail panel and is capped at a fixed height with scrolling. Event rows also switch to a single column.
sections.why: Likely reason: the two-column layout does not fit on a small screen.
sections.watch_out: The fixed height on the step list can hide later steps unless the user scrolls it.

sections.name: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)
sections.title: Reduced motion and replay, evidence and sign-in styles
sections.what: Opens with a rule that stops the animations and colour transitions for users whose devices ask for less motion. The rest of the section styles the replay gate and bar, the evidence document, the header, the sign-in screen, the loading placeholder and keyboard focus outlines.
sections.why: Likely reason: an accessibility setting for people who are sensitive to motion. The other rules are grouped here without a stated reason.
sections.watch_out: The focus outline rule applies across the whole app, so changing it affects keyboard users everywhere.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 767px)
sections.title: Phone rules, print rules and work lanes
sections.what: Adjusts the header, hero text, tool cards, section spacing and workspace header for small screens. A print rule hides the header, buttons and extra tool text and removes the hero picture. The section also styles the three work lanes and the playback bar, and it turns off motion for photos and the loading placeholder.
sections.why: Likely reason: small screens need tighter spacing, and printed pages should drop navigation.
sections.watch_out: The print rule hides the header and action buttons, so anything printed from this view will not show them.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 900px)
sections.title: Work lanes stack on narrow screens
sections.what: Below 900 pixels, the three work lanes stack in one column. The connector between lanes turns from a sideways arrow into a short downward one.
sections.why: Likely reason: sideways connectors do not fit in a single column.
sections.watch_out: The connector position uses fixed pixel offsets, so changes to lane padding can misalign the arrows.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 767px)
sections.title: Narrow screen layout for replay and playback
sections.what: Below 767 pixels, the replay bar and playback controls stack vertically and fill the width.
sections.why: Likely reason: buttons and bars are easier to press when they are in one column on a phone.

summary: The main light-theme stylesheet for the public front page and the workspace pages, covering layout, headers, buttons, tiles and progress views.
purpose: Sets the default look of the site. The dark theme file changes parts of it.
why: The header comment says the design uses dark chrome with light evidence, and that all colours come from shared token values.
how: Covers the front page first: header, hero, buttons, sections, tool grid, perspective block and footer. Then covers the overview and steps, notes, industry banners, sector controls, and the workspace header and scope picker. The pipeline trace begins at the end. Only lines 1 to 120 of 254 were provided, so the later rules, including the media-query rules, are not described here.
inputs: Class names, element names and test-id labels used by the app's components.
outputs: Layout, colours and text sizes for the public and workspace pages.
risks: Many rules depend on shared colour values defined elsewhere. A missing one leaves an element unstyled, with no error. Several workspace rules match test-id labels, so renaming one silently removes its styles. Only part of the file was reviewed.
debug: If a page loses colour, check that the shared colour values exist in the other style files. If a workspace element has no styling, check its test-id label. If a header does not stay at the top while scrolling, check that no parent hides overflow. The rules after line 120 need a separate review.
